title: IB Grade Boundary Changes Explained Over Time
summary: IB grade boundary changes explained: learn why thresholds move between sessions, how to compare years fairly, and how to estimate your IB grade calmly.
body_markdown:
IB grade boundary changes happen because the difficulty of an assessment can vary from one examination session to another. The International Baccalaureate adjusts the mark thresholds associated with grades 1-7 so that, as far as possible, a grade represents a consistent standard of achievement over time. A harder assessment may produce lower boundaries, while an easier one may produce higher boundaries.


That is the direct answer. Yet it can feel less simple when the number belongs to you.


Consider a hypothetical student called Maya. She scores 68% on a Biology practice assessment and immediately searches for last year's boundary. It suggests a 6. Her parent relaxes. Maya does too. But the comparison quietly assumes that the two assessments had the same difficulty, structure, weighting and session context. They may not have.


Historical boundaries are useful evidence, but they are not promises. Understanding that distinction helps students interpret their marks without turning every percentage into a prediction.


### IB grade boundary changes at a glance


Before comparing results, check five things:


- **Subject and level:** Biology HL and Biology SL have different assessment structures.
- **Examination session:** May and November results belong to separate awarding cycles.
- **Assessment year:** Boundaries can move between consecutive years.
- **Component or final subject result:** A component threshold is not necessarily the overall subject threshold.
- **Syllabus and weighting:** A changed course or assessment model can make direct comparison misleading.


RevisionDojo's[IB Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) lets students track thresholds from May 2019 onward. It is the most useful starting point when Maya wants an exact historical conversion rather than a guess based on a screenshot or an undated spreadsheet.


### Why IB grade boundaries move over time


A boundary is a dividing line between two grades. If the lower boundary for a 6 were 68, for example, a final scaled mark of 68 would enter the grade 6 range for that specific subject, level and session. That number is illustrative only. It should not be treated as a current boundary for any course.


The underlying principle is comparability. Two assessments covering the same course can still differ slightly in demand. One may contain an unusually challenging data-response question. Another may make its higher-mark questions more accessible. Fixing the boundary permanently would allow these variations to change the meaning of the grade.


The IB therefore uses professional judgment alongside statistical evidence, grade descriptors and teacher feedback when setting boundaries. The process is more considered than simply examining the average mark and drawing lines around it. RevisionDojo's guide to[how IB grade boundaries are calculated](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-how-theyre-actually-calculated) explores this standard-setting process in more detail.


For Maya, this changes the question. Instead of asking, “What grade is 68% always worth?” she asks, “What does 68% indicate on this assessment, and which historical session is most comparable?” The second question is less satisfying because it contains uncertainty. It is also more accurate.


A student and parent compare a bent historical ruler with an examiner's normal ruler


*An old measuring tool may be informative without fitting the assessment in front of you.*


### What historical changes can and cannot tell you


Historical data reveals a range, not a guaranteed destination. If several comparable sessions placed a grade 7 boundary within a relatively narrow band, that band can support revision planning. It cannot establish the threshold for an assessment that has not yet been awarded.


This is where students often confuse precision with certainty. A table can show an exact figure for May 2024, but its precision applies to May 2024. It does not make the same figure certain for May 2027.


There are also periods when wider circumstances matter. In **May 2021** , the IB publicly stated that its grade-awarding approach would include generosity reflecting pandemic disruption and that appropriate boundaries would be set for different assessment routes. This was an exceptional policy context, not a normal template for future sessions.


In **February 2023** , the IB said it intended the May 2023 distribution of awarded grades to return to pre-pandemic May 2019 levels while still recognizing disruption experienced by that cohort. Again, this dated example explains the context of those results. It should not be used as a prediction for a later session.


Students who want to understand the practical consequences can read[how grade boundaries affect a final score](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-affect-final-score) and the broader discussion of[IB grading and result trends](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/insights-on-ib-grade-boundaries-and-result-trends) . The important habit is to label every historical number with its subject, level and session.


### Raw marks, weighted marks and final IB grades


Maya's next discovery is that her final result may not be a simple percentage average. IB subjects commonly combine several components, and each component contributes according to its prescribed weighting.

This example teaches the calculation only. It does not describe a particular IB subject or establish the grade awarded for a scaled total of 64.


Coursework can therefore matter differently from what a student assumes by looking at raw marks alone. A strong result on a heavily weighted component has more influence than the same percentage on a lightly weighted one. Rounding and subject-specific aggregation rules can also matter near a boundary, so unofficial mental arithmetic should be treated as an estimate.


### How students should use boundaries when revising


The healthiest use of boundary data is to create a margin, not chase a line.


If Maya believes a certain historical threshold is relevant, aiming exactly at that number leaves no protection against marking variation, a harder topic mix or a changed boundary. A sensible target sits above the historical line. How far above depends on the subject, current consistency and time remaining, rather than on a universal formula.


She can then use RevisionDojo's Questionbank to practise targeted skills, Study Notes and Flashcards to repair knowledge gaps, and AI Chat to interrogate an explanation she does not yet understand. Grading tools help reveal where an answer loses credit, while Predicted Papers and Mock Exams provide timed practice. The Coursework Library and Tutors can support longer-term work where feedback and subject-specific guidance matter.


The objective is not to reverse-engineer the lowest mark that might be enough. It is to build performance that remains credible across plausible boundary movement. RevisionDojo also explains[why grade boundaries change each year](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/why-ib-grade-boundaries-change-every-year) , which can help families replace speculation with a clearer revision conversation.


### A calmer way to interpret a borderline mark


When Maya receives another result, she follows a short process:


Step Question to ask


Verify Is this the correct subject, level, session and component?


Convert Have the prescribed component weightings been applied?


Compare What range appears across genuinely comparable sessions?


Add margin Is the target safely above a single historical threshold?


Diagnose Which topics or response skills account for the lost marks?


This process does not eliminate uncertainty. It puts uncertainty in its proper place.


Parents can help by asking about the evidence behind a predicted grade rather than treating one historical boundary as a contract. RevisionDojo's guide to[explaining IB grade boundaries to parents](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/explaining-ib-grade-boundaries-to-parents-35d1b485) offers a useful framework for that discussion.


### Turn the boundary into a planning tool


IB grade boundary changes are not arbitrary movement for its own sake. They are part of an awarding process intended to account for differences in assessment demand while preserving the meaning of IB grades over time.


Maya cannot know a future boundary with certainty. She can know her current strengths, the components that matter most and the amount of margin she has built. That is enough to make the next revision decision intelligently.


For subject-specific historical figures and exact conversions, use RevisionDojo's[Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) . Then move from checking the line to preparing well beyond it.
